basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et respexit Dominus ad Abel et ad munera ejus, ad Cain vero et ad munera illius non'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et respexit Dominus ad Abel et ad munera ejus, ad Cain vero et ad munera illius non respexit. Non enim ait: Et respexit Dominus ad munera Abel et ad ipsum; ad munera vero Cain et ad ipsum non respexit: sed primo personam offerentis acceptam Deo vel non acceptam, deinde munera respecta, vel non respecta esse testatur. Homines etenim saepe muneribus eorum a quibus fuerant offensi placantur; Deus autem, qui est discretor cogitationum et intentionum cordis, nullo magis munere quam pia offerentis devotione placatur: Qui cum puritatem nostrae mentis probaverit, consequenter etiam vota orationum vel operum nostrorum suscipiet
